_: THE CLOSED TABLE. Every name a user-authored formula may call, and there is no other list. DATA, not code, because BOTH lanes read it -- app/src/components/chart/engine/ast/parse.js configures the parser from it and api/services/ast_interpret.py walks the tree it produces. A hand-copy in either lane would be a second grammar, and this repo has already measured what two vocabularies cost: `williams_r` here is `williamsR` in the chart registry, which is why `_CASE_COLUMNS` exists at all.
_shape: FOUR sections. `series` maps a bar-field name to the key it reads. `operators` maps an operator name to its arity -- the canonical tree spells unary minus `u-` and the ternary `?:`, and those names ARE the operator names, not a rendering of them. The functions section maps a name to its argument kinds, its lookback declaration and its read-back sentence. `scalars` maps a per-symbol name to the stored column it reads, the column that DATES it, and its cadence. Every entry in the last three also declares `yields`.
_canonical: The parse->canonical boundary is where this table closes. The persisted tree has FOUR node types -- num, series, op, call -- with keys drawn from {type, name, value, args} and nothing else, so a Python walker has four cases and a surface small enough to prove closed. Anything jsep can produce that has no canonical form (a member read, an array, `this`, a compound, a call of a call) is refused BY NAME at that boundary.
_no_offset: THERE IS NO `ref`, NO `offset` AND NO BACKWARD-INDEX FORM IN v1, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION. A general `close[n]` turns the repaint linter from a lookback SUM into a dataflow analysis, and it makes a FORWARD reference expressible in the first place -- the exact construction (`chikou[j] === close[j+26]`) that the repaint record already names as the thing the linter has to be able to decide. The linter must be simple enough to be obviously right on the day it decides the brand's central claim. Every function below therefore declares its lookback as a constant or as a named argument, so maxLookback(ast) is a tree sum.
_no_offset_reopened_by: Re-opening this is a SPEC decision, not an implementation one: it belongs to the owner of the repaint claim (spec section 4, the phase's repaint-linter task) plus the owner of this manifest, together, because it changes what the linter can decide and what both lane walkers must implement. It is not a v2 feature request that any later task may grant on its own.
_sentence: The read-back sentence lives HERE so that the chip's plain-English phrasing and the interpreter's dispatch come from ONE declaration. A read-back with its own phrase table is a second vocabulary in the same sense the note above describes. `{0}` and `{1}` are argument positions.
_booleans: There is no boolean node type, and the operators section is what forces that: it declares `!`, `&&`, `||` and `?:` over a table whose only literal is a number. A condition is therefore a 0/1 column, and the parser's `true`/`false` literals canonicalise to num 1 and num 0. Both lane walkers must agree on that, and it is asserted in parse.test.js rather than left to each lane to assume.
_yields: `yields` DECLARES WHAT AN ENTRY'S VALUES CAN BE -- `num`, `bool`, or `passthrough` on the ONE entry whose answer is the join of its branches (the ternary `?:`). It is here rather than in a reader because deciding whether a tree is a CONDITION -- a scan is `<ast> != 0` on a 0/1 column, see `_booleans` -- from a hand-list of `which operators are comparisons` is the list-that-rots shape, and it would be hand-listed TWICE, once per language. Declared here, `is_boolean_tree` is derived and a twelfth function is classified the day it lands. ⛔ THE THREE-VALUE SET IS NOT A WIDENING OF THE TWO THE CORRECTION ASKED FOR: `?:` has no static answer at all, and forcing it into `num` would refuse `(a > b) ? 1 : 0` as a scan while forcing it into `bool` would admit `x ? price : volume` as one. A reader that meets `passthrough` resolves it from the branches; a reader that meets an entry with NO `yields` must fail closed to `num`, because refusing to call a tree a scan costs a user an error message and admitting a real-valued tree as one makes `!= 0` true for every non-zero price on the board.
_scalars: A SCALAR IS A DIFFERENT KIND FROM A SERIES AND THE TABLE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN SECTION. `close` is a time series: one number per bar, and the number at bar i is a fact about bar i. `market_cap` is ONE NUMBER PER SYMBOL, dated to a nightly snapshot, and it is the SAME number at every bar of the column -- including at bars that closed before the snapshot was taken. Conflating them is the `chart_settings` vs `charts_workspace_layout` category error: two things with the same shape and different identities.
_scalars_node: A SCALAR RIDES THE `series` NODE TYPE AND THE CANONICAL VOCABULARY STAYS FOUR. `parse.js` turns every identifier into a `series` node deliberately (so the parser needs no table) and resolution is `interpret`'s job; a `scalar` node type would be a FIFTH type in five declaration sites, and every stored tree's `astHash` is taken over `{type,...}` -- so a fifth type is a decision that can never be undone without a migration of every persisted definition. The linter already resolves a DECLARED SCALAR (a definition input) to reach (0,0); a table-declared scalar is the same shape with a wider declaration source.
_scalars_as_of: `as_of` NAMES A COLUMN, NEVER A DATE. Freshness is PER SYMBOL -- one ticker's row can be a month older than another's -- so the declaration points at the row column that carries the value's own date. Two families exist and they are NOT the same date: fundamentals and ratings are dated by `snapshot_date` (when the build ran) and technicals, candles and patterns by `bars_asof` (the newest bar the maths saw). A single as-of would over-claim one family or under-claim the other. Which family each column belongs to is READ OFF `screener/snapshot_builder.build_row`, which sets `bars_asof` only inside the `if bars:` block that fills the technical, candle and pattern groups.
_scalars_freshness: ⭐ THE REPAINT LINTER RETURNS A TRUE ZERO HERE AND THAT IS WHY THERE IS A SECOND VERDICT. A scalar's value at bar i depends on no bar j > i, so `astReach` answers (0, 0) and the repaint gate PASSES `market_cap > 1e9` as non-repainting -- correctly, and uselessly. The zero is a true answer to a question nobody asked. `ast_freshness` / `freshness.js` ask the other one, off THIS section: `live` when no leaf is a scalar, `as-of-snapshot` when one is, `unknown` when a leaf declares something the reader cannot resolve. ⛔ IT IS A CADENCE CLAIM, NOT A STALENESS MEASUREMENT -- how fresh a given symbol's row IS is a per-row runtime fact read off the `as_of` column, and it belongs in a result envelope, never in a badge that would then depend on when it was rendered.
_scalars_totality: ⭐ `scalars` AND `_scalars_excluded` ARE A PARTITION OF `screener/snapshot_db.COLUMNS` -- their union is that list, they are disjoint, and both halves are required. A declared list without the excluded half is a list of what somebody remembered; with the identity, a 66th screener column lands RED until somebody DECIDES about it, which is the only thing that keeps this vocabulary honest as the screener grows. Measured 2026-08-09: 65 columns, 54 declared, 11 excluded. Every excluded entry states WHY, and eight of the eleven state the same reason -- the column is TEXT, and this table's only literal is a number (`_booleans`), so no expression over it is writeable at all.

highest.sentence: the highest {0} of the last {1} bars

lowest.sentence: the lowest {0} of the last {1} bars

pct_vs_sma20.sentence: the percentage distance from the 20-day average

pct_vs_sma50.sentence: the percentage distance from the 50-day average

pct_vs_sma200.sentence: the percentage distance from the 200-day average

pct_vs_ema20.sentence: the percentage distance from the 20-day exponential average

vol_ratio.sentence: the volume ratio against its own average

dist_52w_high_pct.sentence: the percentage distance from the 52-week high

dist_52w_low_pct.sentence: the percentage distance from the 52-week low

above_50sma.sentence: whether the price is above its 50-day average

new_52w_high.sentence: whether the bar made a new 52-week high

body_pct.sentence: the candle body as a percentage of its range

upper_wick_pct.sentence: the upper wick as a percentage of the range

lower_wick_pct.sentence: the lower wick as a percentage of the range

close_position.sentence: where the close sits inside the bar's range

wide_bar.sentence: whether the bar is unusually wide

narrow_bar.sentence: whether the bar is unusually narrow

inside_bar_run.sentence: the run of consecutive inside bars

tight_consolidation.sentence: whether the recent bars are tightly consolidated

pullback_depth_pct.sentence: the depth of the current pullback

higher_lows_run.sentence: the run of consecutive higher lows

nr7.sentence: whether the bar is the narrowest of the last seven

consecutive_up.sentence: the run of consecutive up closes

consecutive_down.sentence: the run of consecutive down closes

_scalars_excluded.ticker: the row's IDENTITY, not a value a formula reads. `ticker == "AAPL"` needs a string literal and this table's only literal is a number
_scalars_excluded.company: TEXT. A name is not a number and the table declares no string literal, so no expression over it is writeable
_scalars_excluded.sector: TEXT, and the one exclusion a user will feel. `sector == "Technology"` is INEXPRESSIBLE here -- granting it means string literals in the parser, both interpreters, the linter and the read-back, which is a phase of its own. Sector filtering stays in the classic screener UI
_scalars_excluded.industry: TEXT, for the same reason as `sector`
_scalars_excluded.exchange: TEXT, for the same reason as `sector`
_scalars_excluded.ma_stack: TEXT -- a rendered arrangement of moving averages, not a magnitude. The individual distances are declared as scalars instead
_scalars_excluded.candle_type: TEXT -- a classification label. The measured components (body, wicks, close position) are declared as scalars instead
_scalars_excluded.patterns: a comma-joined LIST, not a scalar. Expressing membership needs a `contains` this table does not declare; `pattern_conf_max` is the numeric part and IS declared
_scalars_excluded.snapshot_date: an `as_of` SOURCE. Declaring it as a scalar would let a formula compute on its own freshness stamp -- and it is TEXT besides
_scalars_excluded.bars_asof: the same, for the bar-dated family
_scalars_excluded.built_at: an operations timestamp. It dates the WRITE, not the value, so a formula reading it would be screening on when the builder ran
